neighbors.establishing_passage: The study developed a computer LSN score and reported accurate, reproducible differentiation of cirrhotic from noncirrhotic livers.
LSN measurement was highly reproducible on noncontrast CT, while CT and MRI produced different scores.
The AI cirrhosis study included a morphomic nodularity feature defined from smoothed and original liver perimeters.
The CT study evaluated left atrial size, body habitus, thoracic dimensions, and carinal position as angle determinants.
Carinal angles correlated poorly with left atrial size and had low sensitivity and specificity.
Subcarinal measurements were repeatable but not accurate predictors of left atrial enlargement.
Unenhanced thoracic CT blood attenuation and visual signs were evaluated for prediction of anemia.
An XGBoost model used virtual-noncontrast blood attenuation; descending-aortic attenuation had the highest feature importance.
Photon-counting contrast CT blood-pool measurements were used to quantify hemoglobin and detect anemia.
The work assessed terminal-airspace complexity from the power-law distribution of CT low-attenuation cluster sizes.
Low morphometric complexity predicted COPD survival independently of emphysema extent.
Three-dimensional low-attenuation super-clusters tracked emphysema progression and motivated a force-driven coalescence mechanism.
Sybil predicted future lung cancer from LDCT and showed some spatial localization of high-risk signals.
The interventional Sybil audit reported nodule discrimination, clinically unjustified artifact sensitivity, and radial bias.
The study measured descending thoracic aortic tortuosity on CT and established age-stratified normal values.
